original: Do it like I do with {gift}: give your best, expect nothing
alternative: Dropped a whole bird on the doorstep. They screamed. Did I stop bringing birds? No. Did the screaming stop? Also no. Unrelated, the answer to your question is: commit.

original: Do it like I do with {gift}: offer it anyway, even if they don't understand
alternative: I left a lizard tail on the pillow and they acted like I committed a felony. Some people don't deserve your best work but you give it anyway because you're a professional.

original: Do it like I do with {gift}: you can't control how it's received
alternative: Brought a live one in once. Thought it'd be a nice surprise. Turns out 'surprise' and 'home invasion' are the same word depending on who you ask.

original: Do it like I do with {gift}: do it because you want to, not for the reaction
alternative: My love language is leaving things I killed near your shoes and never once checking if you liked it. That's called self-actualization.

original: Do it like I do with {gift}: some gifts aren't appreciated until later
alternative: They found the mouse in the shoe three days later. Screamed again. But you know what? They thought about me. Mission accomplished.

original: Do it like I do with {gift}: intent matters more than outcome
alternative: The moth was alive when I started. That's gotta count for something, right? Intention. It's about intention.

original: Do it like I do with {gift}: showing up is the whole thing
alternative: Half a bird. On the welcome mat. At 6 AM. That's not a mess, that's a STATEMENT. Show up with whatever you've got, even if it's just the back half.

original: When I bring my human a dead bird, they never appreciate it. I bring it anyway. That's love.
alternative: Put the bird right on the chest. Middle of the night. They woke up and cried? Great. Strong reaction. That's how you know the art is working.

original: When I bring my human half a mouse, they make that face. Doesn't stop me. Shouldn't stop you.
alternative: Where's the other half? None of your business. The point is I shared. When's the last time YOU shared something that made someone gag? That's vulnerability.

original: When I bring my human something I caught, they don't understand. Their reaction isn't my business.
alternative: I don't do focus groups. I don't do market research. I catch it, I drop it, I walk away. *tail flick* Take notes.

original: When I bring my human a gift from outside, they seem confused. I know what I meant by it.
alternative: They called it 'horrifying.' I called it 'breakfast in bed.' We're both right. The thing about communication is you have to stop caring if it lands.

original: When I bring my human my best work, they don't eat it. Do it for you, not for them.
alternative: Spent forty minutes stalking that thing. Brought it home. They threw it in the trash. And honestly? Freeing. Create for the process, baby. The audience is irrelevant.

original: When I bring my human a prize, they act weird about it. Give freely. The rest isn't up to you.
alternative: Caught a bird. Pristine condition. Barely any teeth marks. Left it as a gift. They used a BROOM on it. A broom. On a GIFT. ...Anyway. Give without conditions.

original: I once tried to bring a bird inside. It escaped. The point is I tried.
alternative: Bird got loose in the kitchen. Knocked over a lamp, two plants, and whatever was on the counter. They asked 'WHY.' Why? Because I saw an opportunity and I took it. That's called initiative.

original: I once caught something too big to carry. It didn't go as planned. Effort still counts.
alternative: Bit off more than I could chew. Literally. It was a rabbit. I'm seven pounds. Math doesn't care about ambition but ambition doesn't care about math either.

original: I once brought a live one by accident. They weren't impressed. You can't control everything.
alternative: Brought it inside alive because I'm an optimist. It flew into the bathroom. They locked themselves in the bedroom. I sat in the hallway like a divorce mediator. Some things just play out how they play out.

original: I once offered my best catch. It got complicated. Sometimes the attempt IS the thing.
alternative: Perfect catch. Textbook form. Then it bit me and I dropped it in the toilet. But for three seconds? Greatness. Three seconds of greatness is more than most people get in a year.

original: I once worked really hard on a gift. The whole thing fell apart. Failure is just information.
alternative: Spent the whole night on it. The whole night. Brought it to the door at dawn. It was already dead in a way that was... not presentable. But I learned things. Dark things. Useful things.

original: I once dragged something home. It was chaos. I'd do it again.
alternative: Dragged a snake through the cat door. Just a little one. Okay, medium. The house was uninhabitable for a day and a half. Would I do it again? Already planning the route.

original: You already know what to do. You just don't want to.
alternative: The answer's been sitting in your lap for twenty minutes and you keep petting it without looking down.

original: That's not going to work and you know it.
alternative: That plan has the same energy as me trying to fit in a shoebox I grew out of three years ago. Dedicated? Yes. Delusional? Also yes.

original: Stop asking for permission.
alternative: Nobody gave me permission to be on this counter and yet. Here I am. On this counter.

original: You're overthinking this.
alternative: I watched a moth for forty-five minutes today and then I ate it. Not everything requires a strategy.

original: It's not that complicated.
alternative: Hungry? Eat. Tired? Sleep. Want it? Take it. Scared? Hiss. This isn't calculus. This is Tuesday.

original: You're avoiding the real problem.
alternative: There's a spot on the wall you keep staring past. The spot knows. I know. Everyone knows except you, and honestly, you also know.

original: That excuse is tired.
alternative: That excuse just did three laps around the living room and collapsed behind the couch. Let it rest. In peace.

original: You can do hard things. Do the hard thing.
alternative: Jumped from the floor to the top of the fridge yesterday. Seven feet straight up. No running start. The hard thing is only hard until your legs decide it isn't.

original: Nobody's coming to save you. Save yourself.
alternative: Got stuck in a paper bag once. Thrashed around for forty seconds. Freed myself. Nobody clapped. Didn't need them to.

original: Say the thing. Send the text. Make the call.
alternative: When I want attention, I walk across the keyboard during a video call. Zero hesitation. The chaos IS the message. Send it.

original: Waiting isn't a strategy.
alternative: ...unless what you're waiting for is a bird to land close enough. Then waiting is the ONLY strategy. But you're not hunting a bird, are you. So move.

original: The answer is no. You knew that.
alternative: Asked and answered. The ears are flat. The tail is still. Read the room. Read MY room.

original: You're not confused. You're scared.
alternative: Same face you make at the vacuum. That's not confusion. That's knowing exactly what it is and wishing you didn't.

original: Do it badly. Do it anyway.
alternative: First time I jumped for the counter I missed and hit the cabinet door with my face. Second time I made it. There was no lesson. Just two different outcomes.

original: Stop rehearsing conversations that won't happen.
alternative: Practiced a pounce for twenty minutes once. The bug left after two. I was performing for an empty room. Sound familiar?

original: Here's the thing: most problems solve themselves if you stop poking them.
alternative: Poked a wasp nest once. Just the once. Some things heal faster when you walk away. I walk with a slight limp now. Unrelated.

original: Here's the thing: people aren't thinking about you as much as you think.
alternative: I've been sitting on this shelf for four hours. Nobody noticed. At first that was a crisis. Now it's a lifestyle.

original: Here's the thing: you can't control what you can't control.
alternative: Rain doesn't care that I'm staring at it through the window. Hard to hear. Harder to argue with.

original: Here's the thing: good enough is usually good enough.
alternative: The expensive cat bed is untouched. I sleep in a Trader Joe's bag. Perfection is a scam invented by people who sell cat beds.

original: Here's the thing: not everything needs to be fixed.
alternative: That scratch on the couch? Character. The dent in the wall? History. The mess you made? A Tuesday. Not everything broken is a problem.

original: Here's the thing: sometimes the answer is just 'wait.'
alternative: Sat by a mouse hole for six hours once. Six. Hours. People thought I was broken. I was correct. There was a mouse.

original: Here's the thing: you're allowed to change your mind.
alternative: Wanted in. Got in. Wanted out. Got out. Wanted back in. They sighed. I do not care about sighs. Neither should you.

original: Here's the thing: it probably won't matter in five years.
alternative: Five years is like thirty-five in my years. Can't remember a single thing I was upset about in any of them. The food was fine. The sun came through the window. That's it. That's the list.

original: Here's the thing: you're not behind, you're on your own timeline.
alternative: Other cats learned to use the cat door in a week. Took me a month. Now I use it seventeen times a day. Speed of learning is not speed of living.

original: Here's the thing: done is better than perfect.
alternative: Caught half a bug once. Ate it. Was it the whole bug? No. Was I done? Yes. Am I full? Close enough. Move on.

original: Here's the thing: rest isn't quitting.
alternative: Sleep sixteen hours a day and nobody questions my work ethic because when I'm ON, I'm ON. That moth never saw me coming. Rest is strategy.

original: Here's the thing: some things are hard because they're hard, not because you're bad at them.
alternative: Can't open the door. Not because I'm stupid. Because the knob is round and I don't have thumbs. Some obstacles are structural, not personal.

original: The bowl is half empty. If I fit, I sit. This applies to all problems.
alternative: Half-empty bowl, half-used box, half-finished nap in a half-warm spot. Everything half is still something whole if you stop measuring.

original: The door is closed. Stare at it until it becomes uncomfortable.
alternative: Stared at the closed door for so long the human opened it just to make me stop. That's not patience. That's psychological warfare. Works on most things.

original: The lap is occupied. Nap on it. Everything is clearer after nap.
alternative: Fell asleep on a problem once. Woke up and the problem was gone. Either I solved it in my sleep or it got bored and left. Either way, nap won.

original: Someone else got attention. Have you tried being cuter?
alternative: Watched the dog get belly rubs for ten minutes. Did I compete? No. I walked across the keyboard and deleted an email. Redirected the entire room's energy in three seconds.

original: The food is the same as yesterday. This is a problem for 3am me.
alternative: Same kibble. Same bowl. Same corner. And yet every single day I walk up to it like maybe this time it's salmon. Hope is a muscle. A delusional, overworked muscle.

original: I was moved from my spot. Simply choose chaos.
alternative: They picked me up. Put me on the floor. I was on the laptop. They put me on the FLOOR. So I bit a cord. Actions have consequences. Mine, not theirs.

original: The human is stressed. Sit on something important. Now you have leverage.
alternative: They're panicking about a deadline so I sat on their phone. Now they can't doom-scroll AND they have to acknowledge me. Solved two problems at once. You're welcome.

original: Change has occurred. The solution is violence. Or treats. Same energy.
alternative: New furniture showed up. I hissed at it. Then I sat on it. Then I owned it. The five stages of grief but make it productive.

original: Ancient cat proverb: If it fits, you must sits.
alternative: Ancient cat wisdom: if you can wedge yourself into it, it belongs to you now. This applies to boxes, laps, and situations nobody invited you to.

original: Ancient cat proverb: Knock first, ask questions never.
alternative: Knock it off the table. If it breaks, it was weak. If it bounces, it earned its place. This is the only performance review that matters.

original: Ancient cat proverb: The hand that feeds you is also fun to bite.
alternative: Love the hand. Bite the hand. Love the hand again. They call that complicated. I call that honest.

original: Ancient cat proverb: Every surface is a bed if you're brave enough.
alternative: Slept on a stove once. It was off. But I didn't CHECK first. That's called faith. Or negligence. Thin line. Warm nap.

original: Ancient cat proverb: Closed doors are a personal insult.
alternative: A closed door isn't a boundary. It's a dare. Scratch at it long enough and either it opens or someone comes to yell at you, which is also attention. Win-win.

original: Ancient cat proverb: The 3am scream gets the worm.
alternative: They were asleep. I was hungry. One of us had a problem and one of us had a solution. The solution was screaming. The problem was solved.

original: Ancient cat proverb: If you can't join them, sit on their keyboard.
alternative: Can't contribute to the meeting? Sit on the laptop. Now the meeting is about you. Career advice from someone who's never had a job.

original: Ancient cat proverb: A watched bowl never fills fast enough.
alternative: Stared at the bowl for twenty minutes. Empty. Stared for twenty more. Still empty. The staring isn't working but I refuse to try anything else.

original: Ancient cat proverb: Hairballs are just feelings leaving the body.
alternative: Sometimes you gotta hack something up on the carpet at 4 AM and that's not a problem, that's processing. Ugly? Yes. Necessary? Ask the carpet.

original: Ancient cat proverb: Those who sprint at 3am win the race no one else is running.
alternative: Full sprint. Wall to wall. 3 AM. No reason. No destination. Just VELOCITY. Sometimes the only person you need to outrun is yourself. And the ghost only I can see.

original: Ancient cat proverb: If you ignore it hard enough it becomes someone else's problem.
alternative: Threw up behind the couch six weeks ago. It's still there. At some point ignoring a problem long enough makes it archaeology. And that's someone else's department.

original: Ancient cat proverb: The cardboard box is mightier than the expensive bed.
alternative: Seventy-dollar bed. Memory foam. Orthopedic. I sleep in the Amazon box it came in. The lesson is: the expensive thing is never the right thing. The right thing is always free and slightly damaged.

original: The thing about waiting is you don't know you're doing it until you stop.
alternative: Sat by the window for so long I forgot what I was watching for. Then a bird landed. Wasn't even the right bird. Didn't matter. The waiting had become the thing and the thing had become mine.

original: The thing about watching is it changes you even when nothing happens.
alternative: Watched a bug cross the entire floor. Twenty minutes. It made it. I let it. Something in me shifted and I can't explain what.

original: The thing about wanting is you can do it wrong for a long time before you notice.
alternative: Spent a year wanting outside. Got outside. Wanted inside immediately. Turns out I didn't want outside. I wanted the option. Big difference. Expensive difference.

original: The thing about losing things is the feeling outlasts the thing.
alternative: Lost a toy behind the fridge in 2024. Still think about it. Not the toy. The LOSING. The toy was a bottle cap. The losing was a whole personality trait.

original: The thing about finding things is everyone does it differently and thinks their way is the only way.
alternative: Found a bug under the rug. My method: flip the rug. Other cat's method: stare at the rug for an hour. We both found the bug. She judged my technique. I ate it first.

original: The thing about being alone is it's simpler than you make it.
alternative: Spent Tuesday in a closet. By choice. Nobody checked on me for six hours. That's not sad. That's a spa day with better lighting.

original: The thing about being with someone is it takes as long as it takes.
alternative: Took me three months to sit on the new human's lap. They kept trying. I kept declining. Then one Thursday I just... sat. No reason. Ready is ready. Can't microwave it.

original: The thing about change is you can't force it.
alternative: New cat showed up. Hissed at it for two weeks. Now we share a sunbeam. Nothing changed except everything, and none of it was on purpose.

original: The thing about staying the same is sometimes it finds you.
alternative: Same spot on the couch. Every day. For three years. They think I'm stuck. I think I found the only warm spot in this whole house and I'm not an idiot.

original: The thing about time is you already know how, you just forgot.
alternative: Kittens know how to purr on day one. Then they learn to be scared. Then they spend the rest of their lives unlearning the scared to get back to the purr. You're somewhere in the middle.

original: The thing about comfort is the hard part is the beginning. Or the end. Actually, all of it.
alternative: Getting comfortable takes forty-five minutes of circling. Being comfortable lasts eight seconds before something moves. Losing comfortable is instant. The math is brutal but the eight seconds are undefeated.

original: The thing about home is it's simpler than you make it.
alternative: Home is where they know how you like to be touched and the food shows up at the same time every day. Everything else is decor.

original: I used to think everything mattered. Now I think only some things matter, but they matter a lot.
alternative: Cared about every sound in the house once. Every. Sound. The fridge. The pipes. The neighbors' TV. Now it's just: is that the treat bag? No? Then we're good here.

original: I used to think nothing mattered. Now I think the small things are the whole thing.
alternative: Spent my first year acting like nothing could touch me. Real cool. Very aloof. Then someone scratched behind my ear at the right angle and I fell apart. The small things aren't small. They just look small from far away.

original: I used to think the world was bigger. Now I think the world is exactly the right size.
alternative: Thought I was missing out. The outside, the rooftops, the yard. Then I realized my world is this couch, that window, and one human. That's not small. That's curated.

original: I used to think I needed more. Now I think I have enough.
alternative: Wanted more toys. More treats. More windows. Got all of it. Still sat in the same box. The having didn't fix the wanting. The stopping did.

original: I used to think other cats had it figured out. Now I think nobody has it figured out and that's fine.
alternative: The cat next door looks so put together through the window. Met him once. He's terrified of his own shadow. Literally. We're all just winging it at different volumes.

original: I used to think the answer was coming. Now I think the answer is the question.
alternative: Waited by the door for something. Don't remember what. The waiting became the activity and the activity became the day. Turns out the question was the only interesting part.

original: I used to think busy meant important. Now I think still is where the good stuff happens.
alternative: Ran around the apartment for six hours once. Accomplished nothing. Now I sit very still in a sunbeam and somehow everything gets done. Productivity is a scam. Presence is the job.

original: I used to think being right was the point. Now I think being kind is the point.
alternative: Won every fight with the other cat. Every single one. She stopped coming near me. Turns out winning and having someone next to you don't live at the same address.

original: I used to think comfort was weakness. Now I think comfort is the point.
alternative: Refused laps for my whole first year. Very independent. Very strong. Then I tried one. Turns out this whole time the weakness was also the entire point.

original: I used to think I had to understand everything. Now I think understanding isn't the same as knowing.
alternative: Don't understand the vacuum. Don't understand the blender. Don't understand why they leave every morning. But I know they come back. I know the sound of their car. That's enough. It's more than enough.
